single_responsibility.instructions: Does each class, service, and primary unit in the supplied production code own one cohesive responsibility rather than mixing genuinely unrelated architectural or domain concerns?

criteria.pass: Each class, service, or primary unit owns one cohesive role without mixing unrelated domain policies or architectural layers. Private helpers, constants, or supporting types serving that same role pass. Cohesive single-role units also pass: a UI component combining markup, styling, local interaction state, and private sub-components for one view; a focused outbound adapter handling request execution, parsing, telemetry, and error mapping for one external provider; a thin HTTP route handler delegating to services; a storage schema with its record helpers; or a small types/ports file declaring a feature's contracts.
criteria.fail: A class, service, function, or module bundles genuinely unrelated domain concerns or architectural layers so changing one concern requires editing unrelated behavior in the same unit—for example combining business/pricing calculation with report or HTML/CSV formatting, notification delivery, and persistence/retention mechanics, embedding business rules or raw data-fetching inside a UI view, or packing multiple independent workflows or domains into one god-class or monolith.

open_closed.instructions: Does the supplied production code attach variant-specific behavior cleanly so extensions are localized without fragile scattered conditionals, while avoiding speculative hooks?

criteria.pass: Behavior tied to domain variants or types lives with the owning type or a single localized dispatch rather than being duplicated across fragile conditional chains in callers. A single localized adapter handling a small fixed set of external providers or operations, a module exposing distinct named command operations, or straightforward code with no real extension point passes without speculative plugin or registry abstractions.
criteria.fail: Variant-specific or state-machine behavior is scattered or duplicated across repeated or fragile conditional chains or hardcoded caller checks that must all be updated together whenever a variant or phase is added or changed.

liskov_substitution.instructions: Do all subtypes, implementations, and overrides honor their supertype's contract without surprising exceptions, weakened guarantees, or caller type-checks?

criteria.pass: Every subtype, union/sealed branch, or override upholds its supertype's preconditions, postconditions, and invariants without throwing unsupported-operation errors, silently no-oping required behavior, or forcing callers to branch on concrete runtime types. Code without inheritance or interface hierarchies also passes.
criteria.fail: A subtype or implementation breaks its supertype's contract (such as throwing unsupported-operation errors, tightening preconditions, violating invariants, or forcing callers to inspect concrete runtime types or downcast to work around subtype behavior).

interface_segregation.instructions: Are interfaces and collaborator contracts small and focused on what their callers actually use?

criteria.pass: Interfaces and collaborator contracts expose only cohesive operations needed by their callers, with no bloated catch-all interfaces or stubbed/unused methods. Code that defines no custom interfaces also passes.
criteria.fail: An interface or shared contract bundles unrelated methods, forcing implementations to stub out unused operations or forcing callers to depend on broad contracts they do not need.

dependency_inversion.instructions: Do domain objects, application services, and workflows depend on domain values or focused abstractions rather than directly invoking concrete infrastructure or ambient system APIs?

criteria.pass: Domain objects, application services, and workflows depend on domain types, pure values, or focused abstractions rather than directly calling concrete low-level infrastructure or ambient system APIs (such as filesystem, network, database, environment, or system clock APIs). Dedicated infrastructure adapters, persistence repositories (for example under `.server/`), entry points, and composition roots naturally call concrete storage, network, or environment APIs or wire default clock/ID callbacks (`now`, `createId`) at the adapter boundary without adding speculative single-implementation interfaces where passing domain values or a concrete adapter already decouples the policy.
criteria.fail: A domain object, pure domain helper, or application service/workflow (outside a dedicated infrastructure adapter, repository, or composition root) directly instantiates or invokes concrete low-level infrastructure or ambient system APIs (such as filesystem, network, database, environment, or system clock calls) instead of receiving values or depending on a focused abstraction—including when a service or workflow calls a concrete or ambient API directly and passes the result to a domain helper.
